parts:
TikTok and Walmart are taking more control of the purchase. Luxury brands should test platform checkout on margin and repeat purchases before committing to growth.

→ DoorDash plans to acquire Instacart, intensifying competition with Uber and Amazon for fast-delivery shoppers; retailers need to assess the cost of access to those customers.

→ Pandora’s third-quarter organic revenue grew 6%, supported by improved U.S. sales; jewellers testing platform sales should measure contribution alongside revenue.

→ Anthropic reported $17 billion in quarterly revenue and a $23 billion net loss; luxury leaders assessing AI suppliers need to examine losses alongside growth.

#ecommerce #jewelry #retailtech
TikTok and Walmart are moving more of the purchase into their own interfaces. Jewellers should judge platform checkout on margin after fees and returns, before treating it as a growth opportunity.
DoorDash plans to acquire Instacart, intensifying competition with Uber and Amazon for fast-delivery shoppers. For retailers, delivery partners are also competing for the customer relationship.

Pandora reported 6% third-quarter organic revenue growth and narrowed its 2026 outlook towards the top of its previous range. Improved U.S. sales give jewellers evidence of stronger demand in that market.

Anthropic reported $17 billion in quarterly revenue and a $23 billion net loss as its IPO approaches. Luxury businesses assessing AI partners should examine losses alongside revenue growth when weighing supplier risk.

Revolve’s Q3 sales rose 20%, yet profits fell. Logistics costs contributed to the decline. For retailers, the cost of serving customers needs to be part of any assessment of sales growth.
TikTok has launched a standalone TikTok Shop app with in-app checkout. For retailers, app-exclusive deals give shoppers a reason to move into a dedicated shopping app.
One of the world’s largest jewellery retailers closed more than 200 stores. Growth elsewhere could not offset weaker sales in its largest market.
OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company to expand Codex’s software development capabilities. For luxury retailers, that could mean more capable AI tools for ecommerce development.
